To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified mutations in a gene called GAS8 in a family affected by primary ciliary dyskinesis (PCD).

(1) we identified mutations in the GAS8 gene, a gene encoding a subunit of a protein complex called nexin-dyneine regulatory complex (NDR-C), in patients with primary ciliary dysknesia (PCD), an autosomal recessively inherited disease that causes respiratory and fertility disorders; (2) we showed that the corresponding protein is required for the proper localization of another NDR-C subunit called Drc3 and for the alignment of microtubules,
we identified bi-allellic loss-of-function variants in GAS8, which encodes a protein of the nexin dynein regulatory complex (NDRC), in two families with PCD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of ciliary dyskinesis and its consequences for the function of cilia.
the molecular mechanisms of human cilia.
the identification of the genetic cause of a disease, primary ciliary dysknesia (PCD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GAS8 mutations lead to PCD by disrupting the N-DRC complex.
GAS8 is a PCD gene that encodes an N-DRC subcomplex that is important for the proper alignment of the axoneme microtubules.
the nexin-dynen regulatory complex (NDC) is an essential part of the motile apparatus and that mutations in GAS8 lead to a misorganization of axonemae and to the PCD phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mutations in GAS8 cause PCD with axonemal disorganization.
GAS8, a member of a protein complex involved in the regulation of ciliary and flagellar dynein motors, is mutated in PCD patients with a disorganized axoneme phenotype.
GAS8 is required for the proper assembly of the nexin dynein regulatory complex and for the alignment of axoneme doublets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mutations in genes encoding proteins of the N-DRC are associated with ciliary axonemal defects.
the nexin-dynenin regulatory complex (NDC) is a new player in ciliary motility.
mutations in GAS8 lead to a PCD phenotype characterized by ciliary disorganization.
